transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-19
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (DataHarbor CTO), Priya Rao (DataHarbor ML Eng), Sofia Martinez (DataHarbor SRE), Ethan Cole (Infra)

--- Auto Summary (optional):
- Goal: run integrated benchmarks of DataHarbor inference scripts against Redwood hosted/dedicated/private targets, measure latency/throughput/cost, validate streaming outputs and KV cache behavior.
- Success criteria: p95 latency < 300ms for short-chat path, sustained 200 reqs/sec for batch path, cost target <$0.15 per 1k tokens (TBD), no functional regressions vs baseline.

Transcript body:
00:00 - Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, we have arjun and diego from the se team.
00:12 - Liam O'Connor: yeah thanks, um we wanna make sure this POC answers two things, one is can we meet latency targets on our user flows, and two is the cost math at scale.
00:27 - Arjun Patel: great, couple clarifications — when you say latency are we talking streaming or non-streaming? cause that changes the path a lot.
00:35 - Priya Rao: for our chat product the user-visible path is streaming, so partial tokens need to show up within 150-200ms ideally. for batch summarization we can tolerate higher p95 up to 800ms.
00:48 - Diego Ramos: okay, good to know. also, do you have existing harness scripts you run locally today or a load generator?
00:55 - Priya Rao: we have a small python harness, it's a mix, we call a node microservice that streams back incrementally. i'll upload the scripts. sorry if i said node, it's actually golang but, yeah.
01:05 - Maya Chen: perfect, please upload the scripts — earlier we talked about two paths: streaming (partial chunking, SSE/websocket) and non-streaming (single response). for the POC we recommend both, because streaming often trades off slightly higher server complexity for user-perceived latency savings.
01:20 - Sofia Martinez: quick question around KV cache — do you maintain prefix cache across sessions? and does the harness support warm-up sequences?
01:28 - Arjun Patel: our runtime supports prefix/KV cache; for the benchmark we'll want a warm-up phase to populate cache and measure steady state. the harness has options but we'll add a warm-up module if needed.
01:37 - Ethan Cole: firewall/nat question, we'll likely run private tests in our VPC; what are the peering needs?
01:42 - Maya Chen: for private deployment we need VPC peering details and some firewall rules open to Redwood's collector endpoints, we'll send a precise list. for hosted tests we can just run against the hosted endpoint with token.
01:55 - Liam O'Connor: success criteria — i'm thinking: 1) p95 streaming latency <200ms for 95% of dialogs, 2) p95 non-streaming <350ms, 3) throughput 200rps sustained for 1 hour on dedicated pool, 4) cost delta vs current infra <20%. is that realistic?
02:12 - Arjun Patel: seems reasonable as targets to aim for; we'll benchmark multiple model variants and quantization profiles. also want to capture generation quality — we'll run a small eval set to catch regressions.
02:26 - Priya Rao: about quantization, we currently run lightly quantized models on our own infra, curious how Redwood's recommended quant profiles impact latency.
02:34 - Diego Ramos: we'll include quantization matrix in the harness runs. note that some kernels favor int8 vs q4 for certain seq lengths. we'll document.
02:42 - Sofia Martinez: do you support streaming over websockets and SSE? our stack uses websockets mostly.
02:48 - Arjun Patel: yes both; the harness can emulate SSE and websocket streaming. small caveat: measured token-level latency depends on client reassembly and network behavior, so we'll log end-to-end and server-side metrics.
03:02 - Liam O'Connor: ok timeline — we are hoping for a 3 week POC: week 1 infra setup and harness integration, week 2 run benchmarks and iterate, week 3 wrap-up and decision. any blockers?
03:14 - Maya Chen: that's a tight but doable schedule. i'll send the runbook and a checklist today; Ideally we get your scripts by tuesday so se can bake them into the harness.
03:22 - Priya Rao: small note — our dataset has long context docs up to 8k tokens; do you simulate long-context streaming?
03:30 - Arjun Patel: yes we can do long-context paths; it will affect KV cache hits and mem usage. we'll set up a separate long-context test with synthetic warm-ups.
03:38 - Diego Ramos: regarding metrics collection: we'll instrument latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, GPU utilization, token/sec, and cost-estimated based on token counts. we also recommend logging model outputs for a small sample to run diffs against your baseline.
03:52 - Ethan Cole: for private tests we will likely ask for an on-prem image or a docker bundle — is that available?
03:58 - Maya Chen: we have a private deployment package; for air-gapped/on-prem we do a slightly different onboarding — SE team will follow up.
04:06 - Liam O'Connor: security questions — SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs — we need to see docs.
04:11 - Maya Chen: sure i'll attach SOC2 and our security pack; for KMS we support customer-managed keys in private deployments, and audit logs are available in the console.
04:20 - Priya Rao: one more: how do you handle fallback when a streaming path fails mid-response? can the client resume?
04:27 - Arjun Patel: good question — our SDKs provide a resume token and we also have server-side fallbacks to non-streaming for partials. we'll demo that in the harness.
04:36 - Sofia Martinez: testing load pattern — we have spikes to 600rps for 30s then settle to 120rps. can harness emulate sudden spikes?
04:44 - Diego Ramos: yes the harness has ramp and spike profiles; we'll run a 600rps spike test and measure tail latencies and circuit-breaker behavior.
04:52 - Priya Rao: minor nit: our inference script does some post-processing per token, that can affect perceived latency in the UI. we will share the exact step in the scripts.
04:58 - Maya Chen: perfect, that's helpful. to recap next steps: Maya will send harness repo + runbook; Priya to upload scripts and sample dataset; Arjun to draft SLOs and measurement plan; Sofia to confirm VPC/opening rules. we'll aim to kick off infra setup early next week.
05:12 - Liam O'Connor: sounds good, thanks everyone.

Notes and artifacts mentioned:
- Benchmark harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness (will share access)
- Runbook (link to be shared in follow-up)
- Security pack & SOC2 PDF (Maya to attach)
- Benchmark spreadsheet template (Redwood to populate with initial T-shirt sizing)

End of transcript.
